source_name: Digital Europe Programme (DIGITAL) programme page on the Funding & Tenders Portal
why_relevant: DIGITAL funds deployment-stage digital infrastructure (EDIHs, digital identity/EUDI wallet pilots, cloud, AI) — the programme most likely to touch payments-adjacent Czech deployments such as digital identity wallets and instant-payment enablement. Call texts and award lists identify which Czech entities are positioned in these areas.

source_name: Cohesion Open Data Platform (ESIF finance and performance data, incl. Czech programmes)
why_relevant: Shows how much EU cohesion money Czech programmes have allocated and spent on digital/ICT objectives across 2014-2020 and 2021-2027. It sizes the funding envelope that generates the downstream tenders this cell tracks, and flags when a Czech digitalisation programme accelerates — an early indicator of an upcoming wave of IT/payments procurement.

source_name: Národní plán obnovy (Czech Recovery and Resilience Plan) official portal
why_relevant: The RRF-funded Czech recovery plan carries a large digitalisation pillar (public reporting puts roughly CZK 28bn on digitalisation). Its milestone/component reporting names the ministries and state bodies that must procure digital systems — including e-government payment and identity components — which is the upstream signal for TED notices. Czech-language primary source.

source_name: MPO ČR — Národní plán obnovy / OP TAK section (incl. supplier-selection rules)
why_relevant: The Ministry of Industry and Trade runs the business-facing EU digitalisation money (OP TAK, NPO digital calls) that Czech banks' suppliers and fintechs draw on. Its published supplier-selection rules ('Pravidla pro výběr dodavatelů') govern how grant recipients must tender — meaning grant-funded IT purchases become discoverable procurement events even below EU thresholds.

source_name: Věstník veřejných zakázek (Czech Public Procurement Bulletin, VVZ/NIPEZ)
why_relevant: The national gateway through which Czech contracting authorities publish and forward above-threshold notices to TED. Holds the Czech-original text (often richer than the TED summary), the buyer's ICO and the profil zadavatele link to full tender documentation. Essential companion to TED for reconciling a notice to its full Czech document set.

source_name: ISVZ open data (NIPEZ open data on Czech public procurement)
why_relevant: Bulk open data of the Czech procurement information system — supplier names, contract values, CPV, buyer identity. Allows building a Czech-side award history and computing vendor win-share in banking/payments CPV classes, and cross-checking TED completeness for CZ.

source_name: NEN — Národní elektronický nástroj (National Electronic Tool) and Věstník NEN
why_relevant: The e-procurement platform many Czech state bodies run their tenders in, with an English interface available. Carries live tender detail, Q&A ('vysvětlení zadávací dokumentace') and award outcomes — richer than the TED abstract and often the only place the technical specification (e.g. ATM model, terminal certification requirement) is visible, which reveals incumbent vendor lock-in.

source_name: Opentender.eu — Czech Republic portal (TED + national data, analytics)
why_relevant: Third-party normalisation of ~310k Czech tenders combining TED and national sources, with buyer and supplier entity pages and a market-analysis dashboard. Extremely useful as a fast pointer layer: find candidate suppliers/buyers here, then verify each against the primary TED/VVZ notice. Also gives cross-border-supplier views that answer 'which EU vendors bid into CZ'.

source_name: Vhodné-uverejneni.cz — contracting-authority profile directory
why_relevant: One of the certified Czech 'profil zadavatele' hosting services. Acts as a pointer: given an ICO you can locate a buyer's publication profile and thereby the full tender documentation behind a terse TED notice. Snowballing across profiles enumerates state and state-owned buyers relevant to payments (ministries, Česká pošta, customs administration, state treasury).

source_name: Státní pokladna (Czech State Treasury) — payment gateways and payment terminals page
why_relevant: The State Treasury sets how Czech public bodies acquire and operate payment gateways and card terminals, and names the arrangements/providers in use. This identifies the incumbent acquirer/terminal supply relationships across the whole public sector — the commercial context behind any TED terminal or acquiring tender.

source_name: Celní správa ČR (Customs Administration) procurement documents — payment terminal operation contracts
why_relevant: Concrete worked example found in search: a competitive-dialogue protocol for 'Realizace provozu platebních terminálů pro CS ČR' involving ČSOB, published as a PDF on the authority's own site (VVZ form F2017-017645). Demonstrates the pattern that authority websites carry negotiation-stage documents naming the banks/acquirers involved — evidence TED alone never shows. Useful both as a source and as a template for finding equivalents at other authorities.

source_name: Veřejný rejstřík a Sbírka listin (Obchodní rejstřík, Ministerstvo spravedlnosti ČR)
why_relevant: Statutory commercial register plus the Sbírka listin document vault where every CZ s.r.o./a.s. must file annual accounts (účetní závěrka), annual reports (výroční zpráva), auditor reports, articles, merger projects and reports on relations between related parties (zpráva o vztazích). For payment vendors and PSPs this is the primary evidence of revenue, revenue concentration, named key customers, group structure and M&A that marketing never discloses.

source_name: Veřejné rejstříky – nový portál Ministerstva spravedlnosti (verejnerejstriky.msp.gov.cz)
why_relevant: Successor/parallel front-end to or.justice.cz with rozšířené vyhledávání (advanced search) allowing screening by predmet podnikání, address, statutory persons — enables building a population of CZ payment/IT vendors rather than looking up one known name at a time.

source_name: OpenData ISVR – dataor.justice.cz (bulk open data of the Czech public registers)
source_subtype: open data bulk dump / register export
why_relevant: Full-scope bulk XML/CSV dumps of the public registers (since April 2019) — the machine-readable backbone for building a persistent actor map of CZ payment vendors, their statutory bodies, shareholders, capital and address history without scraping the HTML register.

source_name: ARES – Administrativní registr ekonomických subjektů (Ministerstvo financí ČR)
source_subtype: administrative entity register + REST API + open data
why_relevant: Master resolver for CZ legal entities: IČO, legal form, NACE/CZ-NACE activity codes (e.g. 6419, 6499, 6612, 6209), registered address, register linkages. The canonical entity-resolution layer that makes every other filing source joinable, and the way to enumerate firms by payment-related NACE codes.

source_name: Evidence skutečných majitelů (ESM) – beneficial ownership register
why_relevant: Statutory beneficial-ownership register — the only authoritative way to unmask who really stands behind a CZ fintech/PSP behind layered holdings. CRITICAL CAVEAT: the public part was made inaccessible by the Ministry of Justice on 17 December 2025 following CJEU/NSS case law; access now requires data-box self-access, privileged public-authority access, AML-obliged-person request, or proving legitimate interest to a court.

source_name: ČNB JERRS – Seznamy regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů finančního trhu
source_subtype: supervisory register / licence list with web services
why_relevant: Authoritative licence-status layer: which entities hold platební instituce, instituce elektronických peněz, PSMR (poskytovatel platebních služeb malého rozsahu) or e-money issuer permissions, plus passporting notifications. Pairs with justice.cz filings to separate genuinely licensed PSPs from resellers/agents, and to build the competitor universe before pulling accounts.

source_name: Registr smluv (ISRS) – smlouvy.gov.cz
source_subtype: statutory contract register with open-data API
why_relevant: Mandatory publication of contracts above CZK 50,000 by state-owned and public entities — for banking/payments this exposes real supplier relationships and contract values with state-linked banks and public bodies (ČNB, ministries, state agencies, Česká pošta / Poštovní spořitelna ecosystem, ČEB/EGAP). Hard evidence of vendor wins that marketing case studies only hint at.

source_name: Insolvenční rejstřík (ISIR) – eisir.justice.cz
source_subtype: court register / case-file archive with web services
why_relevant: Distress signal on vendors, resellers and fintech competitors: insolvency petitions, creditor filings and full case files since 2008. Creditor lists in an insolvency file are also an indirect customer/supplier map of a failing payments firm.

source_name: Obchodní věstník (ov.gov.cz) – official Czech commercial gazette
why_relevant: Official gazette carrying statutory notices: liquidations, capital changes, general-meeting convocations and (historically) transformation/merger notices. Useful as a time-stamped event feed on CZ payment vendors. Note: the 2024 amendment to the transformations act removed several mandatory OV publications, shifting merger projects into the Sbírka listin instead — so coverage of M&A events has partly migrated.

source_name: CRIBIS (CRIF – Czech Credit Bureau) company profiles
why_relevant: Commercial credit-bureau layer over the statutory registers: financial ratios, payment morale/REPI index, ownership graphs, links to Centrální evidence exekucí and cadastre. Fastest route to a comparable financial scorecard across a set of CZ payment vendors when raw Sbírka listin PDFs are too slow.

source_name: Rejstřík firem Kurzy.cz (rejstrik-firem.kurzy.cz)
why_relevant: Free aggregator of justice.cz data with pre-computed ownership/officer relationship graphs and a browsable Sbírka listin mirror — very efficient for snowballing from one payments vendor to its directors, sister companies and shared shareholders.

source_name: Rejstřík firem Peníze.cz
why_relevant: Second free mirror/aggregator of the commercial register with company profiles, officer histories and financial summaries; useful as a cross-check when one aggregator's parsing of a filing is ambiguous.

source_name: Chytrý rejstřík (chytryrejstrik.cz)
why_relevant: Aggregator adding derived signals — estimated revenue (tržby), risk flags, vehicle fleets, contacts — on top of register data; a cheap proxy scale indicator for small CZ payment vendors that file abbreviated accounts.

source_name: European e-Justice Portal – Business Registers Interconnection System (BRIS)
why_relevant: Single EU entry point (live since June 2017) into all Member State business registers plus Iceland/Liechtenstein/Norway, with EUID identifiers, cross-border branch and cross-border merger notifications. The route from a CZ subsidiary of a payments vendor to its foreign parent's home register — and vice versa. Note it exposes only basic harmonised data, not filings or financials.

source_name: GLEIF – Global LEI Index
why_relevant: Free bulk LEI reference data including Level-2 'who owns whom' direct and ultimate parent relationships. For CZ banks, PSPs and payment institutions with an LEI, this gives a machine-readable group-structure skeleton to validate against register filings, and a stable cross-border identifier joining CZ IČO to foreign parents.

source_name: UK Companies House – filings of foreign parents of CZ payments vendors
why_relevant: Many payment vendors, acquirers and fintechs active in CZ are UK-parented or have UK holding entities; UK group accounts frequently disclose segment revenue, CEE subsidiary lists and acquisitions in far more detail than the Czech subsidiary's abbreviated accounts. Free full-text filing search plus a public REST API.

source_name: Bundesanzeiger / Unternehmensregister (Germany) – parent and DACH group filings
why_relevant: German-parented payment/banking technology groups (and Austrian/DACH holding structures serving CZ) publish Jahresabschluss and Konzernabschluss with subsidiary lists (Anteilsbesitzliste) naming their Czech entities — evidence of group ownership and CEE segment performance not visible in CZ filings.
